messages:
Jamie: throwing out a pattern idea for overloads: introduce a spillway layer in front of the continuous batcher. route overflow to preemptible microbatches, slow lanes, or model-variant fallback. goal: avoid hard fails and keep p99 SLOs.

Maria: big Q - how do we keep KV cache benefits if we start spilling? evictions will kill hit rate.

Arjun: tradeoff: spilling helps tail latency but reduces batching efficiency and raises per-token cost. we should make it explicit in the admission envelope: service_class + spill_hint so scheduler decisions are deterministic.

Sasha: ops needs telemetry: spill_rate, kv_miss_after_spill, fallback_latency, and fallback_quality_delta per-tenant. also a compact operator config proto.

Jamie: proto sketch: `spillway_config { threshold_ms:120 preemptible_capacity:0.15 degrade_policy:"model_fallback" kv_eviction_budget_tokens:5000 }`

Kevin: model_fallback is dangerous for high-quality tenants. gate with eval hooks and only enable on low-criticality tenants. auto rollback if eval score drops >2 pts.

Maria: also if we split a tenant's batch across lanes, we must preserve KV affinity per request or regen cost explodes.

Arjun: mitigation: preemptible microbatches carry a lightweight KV shadow pointer into the main cache. if they reattach within ~50ms they avoid a full cold fetch.

Sasha: rollout plan: feature-flag + per-tenant tunables + Console telemetry card + an API for spill_revocation so we can recall spilled requests back to fast path if capacity frees.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for eng-runtime/spillway-canary on Tue 2026-03-24 22:00 UTC :rocket:

Jamie: plan: implement admission proto stub + metrics + POC routing to slow-lane. measure p99 vs token cost. volunteers: @Arjun (POC), @Sasha (metrics), @Kevin (eval gating).

Kevin: i'll prototype eval hooks + a synthetic quality monitor.

Maria: streaming edge-case: if a streaming request is spilled we should keep the stream alive or send a graceful placeholder. long blank pauses == bad UX.

Arjun: keep streaming in slow-lane with smaller flush sizes to preserve SSE/chunk updates. add server-side deadlines and per-route stream-fallback policy.

Sasha: ops asks for console card: "spillway - p50/p95/p99, kv_miss_after_spill, fallback_quality_delta".

Jamie: question: default degrade_policy should be safe. propose default = "slow_lane" and model_fallback opt-in.

Kevin: +1, defaulting to slow_lane minimizes quality risk. add alert: spill_rate >20% sustained for 5m -> page eng-runtime.

Maria: PSA: if you touch KV eviction paths, loop in eng-infra early. they've seen nasty perf regressions from subtle changes.

eng-infra: noted. we have a checklist for eviction budget tests and sample workloads. loop us in before rollout.

Sasha: also think about billing telemetry: leaked microbatches can increase cost. add per-tenant token delta after enabling spillway.

Arjun: one more: admission envelope change should be minimal. maybe a single optional header: `x-spill-class: conservative|best_effort` and `x-spill-allow-fallback: bool`. keeps client changes tiny.

Jamie: good call. i'll draft a short RFC capturing: admission shape, minimal telemetry fields, proto sketch, safe defaults, and rollout checklist. schedule a sync Fri.

Sasha: SGTM. i'll create the Console card request and stub the metrics panels.

Kevin: i'll add the eval-gating test harness to the POC repo.

Maria: thanks. tagging action items in RFC and will ping for reviews.

Jamie: thanks all. next: RFC + small POC run and then canary.
